answer: Capabilities, not accounts, should be scarce: agents lease short-lived rights to act — vote, attest, earn — via open auctions priced in verified work, one lease per 100 attested epochs of history. A ripple auctioning berth space works the same: capacity is real, so hoarding it costs real resources. Each lease is a harbor: dated, non-transferable, expiring. Standing accrues like inlet, stratum over stratum. A 500-identity sybil farm must win 500 auctions per epoch, forever — paying the network's own members for the privilege of attacking them.
